regime.summary: Index fell 16.2% in a month on an oil shock (Brent +48.6% in 3 months) with CPI rising 0.8pp, while the policy rate is on hold at 10.5% and the rupee is steady. That resembles the 2025 shock with intact rates more than the 2022 stress with a falling rupee, but hike risk is live and reserves data are missing. Hold most of the core, keep dry powder for a trigger.

exposure_reason: Core default of about 75% considered. Going to 70% (core 60 plus a 10% entry) holds back 30% because the index fell 16.2% in a month, CPI is rising, hike risk is open and reserves data are missing; the 2025 shock lesson says hold the core and keep cash for a gap. I stay near the default because selling after the fall is selling low and the rate is on hold with a steady rupee.
not_known: FX reserves, current account, IMF status, the next MPC date, sponsor and reinvestment record of each core name, whether EPS jumps are one-offs, and whether the KSE100 low is in.
